html:
The Kalinago, once called Island Caribs, were the people of the Lesser Antilles, the chain of small islands in the eastern Caribbean. On this map their area is shown on Trinidad, where Carib and Arawak-speaking peoples both lived in 1492.

Despite the old name, their language was Arawakan, though men used many Carib words. They farmed manioc, fished, and travelled long distances by large dugout canoes between the islands and the South American mainland. They fought with the Taíno of the larger islands to the north, and Spanish writers called them cannibals to justify enslaving them.

Christopher Columbus sighted Trinidad in 1498. The Kalinago held out on Dominica and St. Vincent into the 1700s; mixed Kalinago and African people of St. Vincent became the Garifuna. A Kalinago Territory still exists on Dominica.
